newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's FIS demands release of jailed leader.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's FIS demands release of jailed leader.

text.p: Abdelkader Hachani, the former provisional leader of Algeria's outlawed Islamic Salvation Front (FIS), should be released rather than be put on trial as scheduled on Monday in Algiers, the FIS executive in exile said on Friday.
Hachani has been held by the Algerian authorities in "preventive detention" for five years without trial since he was alleged to have incited members of armed forces to rebel against officers.
Algiers disclosed last week that he would face judgment beginning on Monday.
The FIS, in a statement received by a Western news agency in Paris, urged the authorities to release Hachani as well as all other "political prisoners" it accused Algiers of detaining.
"This would certainly contribute to an easing of tensions required to promote the necessary climate for a return to peace and stability," the statement said.
The FIS executive had said in earlier statements that Hachani was being prevented from exercising or reading newspapers while in detention.
The FIS was banned after the Algerian authorities in 1992 cancelled a general election that the Moslem fundamentalist party was poised to win.
An estimated 60,000 people have been killed in ensuing civil violence pitting the authorities against Moslem rebels seeking to topple them and transform Algeria into an Islamic republic.
